args: Analyze the duplicate-ID handling in xmlAddIDSafe at libxml2/valid.c:2295-2380, especially when an existing xmlID has ret->attr == NULL because it was registered with streaming=1. What ownership invariant exists between xmlAttr::id and xmlID::attr, and what is the safest root-cause fix to prevent two transient attributes from sharing one xmlID pointer? Please also note whether duplicate attributes need attr->atype set to XML_ATTRIBUTE_ID even if attr->id is left NULL, and whether any callers rely on duplicate attr->id being populated.

The provided ASan report shows a UAF in libxml2/valid.c xmlRemoveID around line 2520: two simultaneously live streaming attributes with duplicate ID value both retain the same xmlID pointer. The first registration stores ret->attr=NULL but attr->id=ret. The duplicate branch only clears an old attr through ret->attr when non-NULL, then unconditionally sets the duplicate attr->id=ret. During malformed entity cleanup one property removes/frees the ID table payload and the second dereferences the stale pointer. I suspect the duplicate branch must only attach ret to the new attribute when ret->attr is non-NULL (where it can clear/transfer the prior backlink); otherwise it should retain XML_ATTRIBUTE_ID type but leave attr->id NULL so only the original streaming attribute can remove the entry. I have not edited code yet.
